title: 2015_PMC4640112_Febrile_seizures_after_2009_influenza_A_H1N1_vaccination_and_inf
ehr_evidence: In addition to information from the national population registry, we used information from the Norwegian Directorate of Health, the Norwegian Surveillance System for Communicable Diseases, the Norwegian Immunisation Register, and the Norwegian Patient Register.
summary: Nationwide registry-based self-controlled case series study estimating the risk of febrile seizures in Norwegian children following 2009 H1N1 influenza vaccination or infection.
key_findings: The incidence rate ratio (IRR) of febrile seizures 1–3 days after vaccination was 2.00 (95% CI: 1.15–3.51).
No increased risk of febrile seizures was observed in the period 4–7 days after vaccination.
The IRR of febrile seizures on the same day as a diagnosis of influenza was 116.70 (95% CI: 62.81–216.90).
A tenfold increased risk was observed in the period 1–3 days after a diagnosis of influenza (IRR 10.12, 95% CI: 3.82–26.82).
population: 226,889 Norwegian children born 2006–2009 (up to 45 months old) resident in Norway as of October 1, 2009
limitations: Lack of validity testing for outcome diagnosis
Under-ascertainment of influenza cases in primary care
Results likely apply to more severe influenza infections
